schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The nest: a shared machine made of sieve tools (outline 16.2). Each question is a sieve; sieves can come after others. Bands are phases: preprocess, measure, postprocess. nest(reaches) assembles the bands coarsest-first with empty bands omitted; shake(assembled, subjects, fire) runs them band-outer: a preprocess sieve receives the whole subject set and returns the subset to score, a measure sieve receives one subject, a postprocess sieve receives one subject and the stamps of every subject so far, so a compare over all the inputs (the cheapest survivor) runs inside the nest. Scores are 0.0 or 1.0, a sieve that did not fire is absent, the roll-up is min(). The band a sieve sits in is derived from what it reads (import_sieve.phase_of), never authored.
why: Outline 16.2.2: questions that can be answered deterministically should never reach an LLM; a nest composes those questions so routing and inspection run without inference. Outline 16.2.4: its users are the inference proxy's route machine (11.4.6) and build_inspector (9.4.3), two components, so it is a shared machine under cairn/machines/ (outline 16), not a file inside the base tool. Akien 2026-09-15: the bands were built for the inference proxy, 'to pick the least expensive of the paths provided' — 'a different kind of compare operation performed on all the available inputs. if it's not like that now, that's a bug.'
falsifier: A shake fires a postprocess sieve before every measure sieve has fired over every subject; a postprocess sieve does not receive the stamps of all subjects; BAND_NAMES names band 1 anything but measure; or a tenant's findings change bytes when the shake changes order.
learns: It does not learn: it holds no state. Its tenants own what they learn from a shake.
